messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] High GPU queue growth — autoscaler failed to scale past 85% due to placement fragmentation. Alert: GPU queue length > 12k, throttle events rising. Incident created: INC-2026-4989991111. Link: <https://redwood/incident/4989991111>

devon (oncall): I'm on it. Paging SREs. @maria can you take GPU scheduler?

maria (sre): on it, grabbing logs.

kevin (infra): seeing a lot of "no matching MIG slot" errors in allocator -> binpacking failing. likely due to mix of 1g/2g/4g MIG sizes. snapshot of allocator log:

```
allocator: failed to place job seq=... reason="no-matching-mig-slot" counts: 1g:120/160,2g:0/32,4g:4/8
```

maria (sre): yeah fragmentation: a bunch of 1g slices empty but larger jobs need 4g. autoscaler is at max replicas (maxPool=200) and cannot get contiguous capacity. queue growing.

devon (oncall): what's customer impact? sally?

sally (support): Support: approx 18 customers reporting timeouts on gen api. Top impacted: fintech-prod, search-realtime (high qps). ETA for workaround?

maria (sre): quick mitigation plan:
- accept lower throughput by temporarily allowing MIG-slicing fallback (risk: perf)
- emergency evict low-prio burstpool to free contiguous 4g allocations
- lift autoscale max to 250 as stopgap and request more capacity from cloud
I'll run eviction script in 2min if no objections.

kevin (infra): cloud quota request pending but slow. Eviction ok. How to avoid noisy neighbor? use label selector "burstpool=true".

devon (oncall): do it. I'll open customer comms and post in #general-support. Notify legal if any regulated customers.

maria (sre): running:

```
./tools/evict-burstpool --label burstpool=true --modes=drain --selector 'priority=low' --dry-run=false
kubectl get pods -l burstpool=true -o json | jq '.items | length'
```

maria (sre): eviction started. current queue: 12,450 -> 9,100 in 5m. throttles decreased. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: autoscaler: attempted scale to 240 but bounded by maxReplica=200. override applied by devon to 260. autoscaler triggered scale up -> requested 60 more nodes.

kevin (infra): requested extra MIG shapes in cloud; provisioning ETA 7-12m.

devon (oncall): coordinate handoff to night oncall at ts 4989991440. @maria please prepare summary.

maria (sre): summary prepared. root cause: fragmentation from mixed MIG sizes + leftover 1g slices after recent canary deploy; autoscaler couldn't pack larger gpu jobs -> stranded capacity. Action items: temporary evict, increase maxReplica, follow-up: schedule background repack job to defragment pools, add autoscaler smarter binpacking heuristic. :memo:

sally (support): posting update to affected customers: "We're investigating GPU capacity issues, some requests are delayed. We're applying temporary mitigations, more updates in 10m." Link to status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/4989991111

devon (oncall): incident status: mitigated -> partial recovery. queue 2.3k and falling. Will stay in pager loop until cloud nodes are active and repack completes. escalate if queue rises >5k.

maria (sre): note: we saw one failure in the delete/evict flow: "eviction timeout" for pod id abc123 — retried and succeeded.

kevin (infra): creating follow-up ticket: INFRA-6421 "MIG sizing audit and repack automation". assignees: kevin, maria.

devon (oncall): handing off to night oncall ravi (oncall). @ravi please monitor queue and autoscaler logs.

ravi (oncall): ack. i'll watch and will ping if >5k or errors reappear. :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident closed to page after 2h; severity downgraded; follow-up ticket created INFRA-6421. tags: gpu, fragmentation, autoscale. :white_check_mark:

sally (support): thx team. I'll follow up with customers with postmortem link when ready.

everyone: :rocket:
